verdict.condition: Do not launch the app or agent in QA mode against real services until all critical containment findings are fixed and independently reverified.

adversarial_probes.name: parent_symlink_path_escape
adversarial_probes.method: Create run/link as a symlink to a temporary outside directory, resolve --database run/link/escaped.sqlite, write through the accepted URL, and confirm outside/escaped.sqlite exists.

findings.title: QA path containment is bypassable through an existing parent-directory symlink
findings.impact: A supposedly isolated database, Screenwatch, Application Support, or export path can write outside the QA root, including into production state if an attacker or broken harness prepares the symlink.
findings.recommendation: Reject symlink components with file-descriptor based containment or resolve and validate an existing parent directory immediately before opening each output.

findings.title: QA mode does not prevent selection of production roots or production identity domains
findings.impact: A QA root can be the user's real Library directory, and QA accepts the production UserDefaults suite name. The guard proves relative containment only, not separation from protected production locations or identities.
findings.recommendation: Require QA roots beneath an approved dedicated base, reject overlap with home, Library, Application Support, Screenwatch, installed app, and production database paths, and forbid production or cross-run suite and Keychain identifiers.

findings.title: Sensitive app consumers bypass RuntimeEnvironment and remain connected to production state
findings.impact: A QA app still uses the production Mach service, settings database defaults, App inventory database default, capture configuration, Keychain service, standard UserDefaults, notifications, microphone and global hotkey, and ServiceManagement registration path.
findings.recommendation: Create one dependency container from RuntimeEnvironment and inject it into AppModel, Settings, voice, XPC, ServiceManagement, capture, inventory, notification, and external-source consumers. QA mode must fail closed when a production consumer is requested.

findings.title: The QA agent still uses production macOS integrations and production capture configuration
findings.impact: QA startup can read real Reminders, use real Calendar and notification adapters, accept permission-request flags, start the parent app, and use production native-capture configuration and directories. Seeded QA outbox work could mutate real EventKit.
findings.recommendation: Require fixture adapters in QA mode, prohibit permission and ServiceManagement operations, derive native capture configuration and directories from the QA root, and use a unique QA Mach service.

findings.title: Scenario validation does not enforce the committed JSON Schema or evidence referential integrity
findings.impact: The validation command accepts a wrong schema version, wrong schema URI, wrong tracker path, unexpected top-level properties, nonexistent verified commits, arbitrary build IDs, and impossible evidence line numbers.
findings.recommendation: Validate the entire payload against the committed schema, resolve verified commits in Git, validate build identity format and provenance, and verify evidence files and referenced line bounds.

findings.title: All six checked scenarios require proof classes but have no evidence paths
findings.impact: The registry can report fully implemented checked scenarios while its machine-readable proof linkage is empty, so it cannot independently support a release gate.
findings.recommendation: Require at least one immutable evidence manifest for checked scenarios and verify that every required proof class is satisfied by typed evidence records.

findings.title: Fifteen downgraded scenarios retain old verification commit and build metadata
findings.impact: Historical verification metadata survives a checkbox and status downgrade, which can be mistaken for current completion proof unless consumers understand the status field takes precedence.
findings.recommendation: Separate historical verification from current accepted proof, or clear current-verification fields whenever checkbox, status, disposition, or required proof changes.
